title: s5n values
description: One release = one namespace = one seedbox. Fields here are the contract the templates and the wiring Job both read; anything not described fails the install rather than rendering something surprising.

theme.description: The palette `box` draws its dialogs in, read from this file when box starts on the host. The chart renders nothing from it; every name is one internal/theme accepts, and a pair name follows the terminal's background while a variant name pins one.

login.description: The account root's own login admits, written here by box from the grant. The chart renders no login of its own; it is here because an app that keeps its own accounts (Jellyfin) names the person's first account after it, so the box has one name to teach them. No values file may set it.

rehearsal.description: A rehearsal box: no public-internet egress, proven from inside the namespace before any app starts. box sets it in the grant when it applies a rehearsal snapshot, and no file may set it; a rehearsal box is disposable and the real run starts from a final snapshot on a clean host.

rehearsalGate.description: The in-cluster address (host:port) a rehearsal box's apps wait on in an init container until the lock closes it. box writes it into the grant with rehearsal; no file may set it.

puid.description: uid every app runs as, and the owner of /data.

auth.description: Who checks the login in front of this release. The chart ships no login; auth.edge is the operator's explicit statement that one is there, and there is no default.

edge.description: Must be true. The chart refuses to render when it is missing or false: a release whose admin apps nobody signs in to is not one this chart installs. box sets it.

oidc.description: How an app in this release reaches the login as an OIDC issuer. The login advertises the URL the browser used (https://<gateway.host>/auth), so an app pod has to reach that name like a browser does: box reads the Gateway's proxy address from the cluster and writes it here, and the chart gives the app's pods a hostAliases entry for it. Absent on a release from before the provider, and the app then renders without it.

gatewayIP.description: The ClusterIP of the Service in front of the Gateway's proxy, which is what answers for the box's own name inside the cluster. box writes it from the grant; neither file may set it.

storage.description: The claims the release mounts. Both must already exist; the chart creates no storage. Create them before helm install (box creates them from the grant's host paths).

host.description: Public hostname. Empty matches any host.

tls.description: TLS issuer for this seedbox. The chart renders nothing from it; box init reads it, and an empty value lets init decide from the domain.

apiServerCIDRs.description: Fallback for the wiring Job's API-server egress when the chart cannot look the endpoint up (offline rendering).

existingSecret.description: Use a pre-made Secret instead of generating one. It must hold <instance>-apikey keys and qbittorrent-password.

plexToken.description: Optional Plex server token (X-Plex-Token), mounted as the Secret's plex-token key and given to Tautulli. Empty leaves tautulli/plex pending; Plex never trusts a network range instead.

plexClaimToken.description: The claim token from plex.tv/claim, mounted as the Secret's plex-claim-token key. It expires minutes after issue, so box init asks it last and passes it to one apply instead of writing it to a file. Plex only uses it while the server is unclaimed.

apps.description: One entry per catalog app. Every key here is a workload: s5n.instances builds the workload list from these keys, so adding an app means adding a key here and in this schema (additionalProperties false is what keeps a non-app key out), never editing a template.

port.description: Externally reachable peer port, and the one key this chart ships no default for: box picks a free port in the lower band of the NodePort range and records it in the grant, and a helm install must set it (the render refuses without it). With a NodePort service it must also sit in the cluster's NodePort range; with LoadBalancer the LoadBalancer implementation assigns the address.

annotations.description: Annotations applied to the peers Service, e.g. metallb.io/allow-shared-ip or metallb.io/loadBalancerIPs.

noAuthNetworks.description: CIDRs allowed to reach Plex without a Plex.tv account token (PLEX_NO_AUTH_NETWORKS). Empty by default: the Gateway reaches Plex from a pod IP, so a trusted range would expose the server unauthenticated.

knownProxies.description: The peers whose X-Forwarded-For Jellyfin honours (network.xml KnownProxies), as addresses or subnets. Empty makes the app ignore the header, so every request through the Gateway counts as local; box writes the cluster pod network here from the Nodes' podCIDRs at init, and the chart puts it in network.xml before the app starts because the app reads it once.

digest.description: Optional image digest, pinned alongside the tag.

image.description: A blessed image variant, by name. The repository comes only from the chart's variants.yaml; a user may pin a tag or a digest inside that variant's repository.

variant.description: A variant name from the chart's variants.yaml (apps.<app>.image.variant).

tag.description: Optional tag pin inside the variant's repository. It replaces the variant's tag, and drops the variant's digest unless a digest is pinned too.

claim.description: A claim that already exists. The chart creates no PersistentVolume and no claim: create the claim before helm install (box does this from the grant's host path).

existingClaim.description: Name of an existing PersistentVolumeClaim in the release namespace. Create it before helm install; the chart creates no storage and has no host path, storage class or size setting.

suffix.description: Appended to the app name: sonarr + "4k" = sonarr-4k. Empty for the primary instance.

category.description: The directory this instance's library lives in under /data/media, and its download directory unless downloadCategory says otherwise. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' per segment, with at most one '/' for a subcategory (4K/Movies); the parent directory is created too.

downloadCategory.description: The qBittorrent category this instance downloads into, and the /data/downloads directory behind it. Defaults to category; a migrated box keeps the source's own, because its torrents are already there.

suffix.description: Appended to the app name: bazarr + "4k" = bazarr-4k. Empty for the primary instance. The instance reads the Sonarr and Radarr with the same suffix, so bazarr-4k is sonarr-4k and radarr-4k.
